extracted.intended_audience: readers, students, and scholars of contemporary Chinese literature and general readers seeking an author biography
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia-style author biography and overview of Mo Yan's life, major works, themes, influences, style, and critical reception. Useful for readers seeking descriptive criteria about his writing and career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hallucinatory realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Works characterized as 'hallucinatory realism' that merge folk tales, history and the contemporary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Nobel Committee described his work as 'with hallucinatory realism merges folk tales, history and the contemporary.' Hallucinatory realism is presented as a defining stylistic mode for evaluating Mo Yan's fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epic historical scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Novels are often epic historical narratives spanning decades and addressing major historical upheavals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Red Sorghum (generations between 1923 and 1976) and Life and Death Are Wearing Me Out (chronicles life from land reform to contemporary China). Evaluate works by breadth of historical sweep and integration of personal/family saga with national history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of black humour
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent incorporation of black humour into novels and stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mo Yan's works are described as 'epic historical novels characterized by hallucinatory realism and containing elements of black humour.' Assess presence and effect of darkly comic tone alongside serious themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaginative use of colour expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Language distinguished by imaginative and vivid colour imagery and expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes his 'imaginative use of colour expressions' as a notable linguistic feature; evaluate descriptive language, sensory vividness, and novel metaphors involving colour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic and dazzling imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of dazzling, complex, and often graphically violent images in scenes and descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The biography highlights 'dazzling, complex, and often graphically violent images' as stylistic traits; when judging effectiveness, consider how stark or visceral imagery supports themes rather than gratuitously shocking readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predominant social commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Works function largely as social commentary on greed, corruption, and the interaction of ideology and society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A major theme is 'the constancy of human greed and corruption, despite the influence of ideology.' Evaluate how plot, character, and satire deliver social critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blurring of temporal and moral boundaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Blurring of distinctions between past and present, dead and living, and between good and bad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page states his writing 'is characterised by the blurring of distinctions between "past and present, dead and living, as well as good and bad".' Assess narrative techniques (nonlinear time, reincarnation, magical elements) that create this effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local setting rooted in Gaomi
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories frequently set near his hometown, Northeast Gaomi Township, Shandong Province.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many works are anchored in Gaomi; evaluate how local detail, dialect, customs, and rural community life contribute to authenticity and thematic resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence of magical realism and social realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Stylistic and thematic influence from Gabriel García Márquez (magical realism) and Lu Xun (social realism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The biography links Mo Yan to Faulkner and García Márquez and contrasts magical realism with social realism influences; assess interweaving of mythic/magical elements with social critique and realist observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of folklore, classical and oral traditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspiration and formal borrowings from classical Chinese literature (Water Margin, Journey to the West, Dream of the Red Chamber), Six Dynasties chuanqi, Ming/Qing notebook novels, and folk oral literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page emphasizes deep roots in Chinese traditional forms and oral storytelling; assess incorporation of motifs, narrative forms, episodic structures, and folkloric voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satirizing socialist realism by absurd situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Satire of socialist realism achieved by placing workers and bureaucrats in absurd or exaggerated situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mo Yan 'satirizes the genre of socialist realism by placing workers and bureaucrats into absurd situations.' Evaluate comedic/satiric inversion of official narratives and how absurdity exposes contradictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of shocking metaphors and transgressive devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of transgressive imagery and metaphors (e.g., cannibalism) as extended metaphors for social or cultural critique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: The Republic of Wine 'uses cannibalism as a metaphor for Chinese self-destruction.' When judging, consider whether shock serves allegorical purpose and thematic coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semi-autobiographical self-insertion
rubrics_metrics.description: Author frequently appears in his novels as a semi-autobiographical character who retells and modifies stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes Mo Yan 'appears in his novels as a semi-autobiographical character'; evaluate narrative reliability, metafictional effects, and the role of authorial presence in shaping perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nontraditional portrayals of gender and female bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Female characters often subvert traditional gender roles and are central to contentious depictions (e.g., Big Breasts & Wide Hips).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The biography cites examples of female characters who defy norms; evaluate complexity, agency, and how bodily imagery is used to interrogate gender and history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Productive practice: preference for handwriting
rubrics_metrics.description: Mo Yan prefers writing novels by hand rather than typing with pinyin input, claiming typing 'limits your vocabulary.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a stated production habit linked to craft and diction; consider how method (handwriting vs. typing) might influence lexical range, rhythm, and drafting practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive voice formed by multiple influences
rubrics_metrics.description: A distinctive, hybrid authorial voice resulting from combining global modern influences (Faulkner, García Márquez) with Chinese classical and folk traditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page claims his 'creation combines all of these inspirations into one of the most distinctive voices in world literature.' Evaluate originality in synthesis of influences, tonal consistency, and voice recognizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid and voluminous composition in some works
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of rapid composition (e.g., Life and Death Are Wearing Me Out written in 42 days and composed on traditional paper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noted as part of biography; when assessing craft, consider whether speed of composition affected structural or stylistic features (coherence, density, spontaneity).
